sources.title: NASA’s Hubble Telescope Reaches Milestone, Looks for Elusive Supernova

discussion.body: The prediction window is the part worth watching. Astronomers already have one sighting of Athena; a second arrival gives them an interval to compare against models of the cluster doing the lensing.
Keep the chain of inference in view: time the reappearances, infer the lens mass, and only then say something about expansion. The expansion claim is the last link, not the first.

items.title: One Supernova, Two Appearances, and a Measurement of the Universe's Expansion
items.body: Supernova Athena, discovered by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope in 2025, is predicted to reappear between now and early March 2027. The reason for a second showing is the foreground: the galaxy cluster MACS J0417 acts as a gravitational lens, bending and magnifying light from objects far behind it. NASA says measuring the timing of Athena's reappearances can help researchers map the mass of that foreground lens and refine our understanding of the expansion rate of the universe — so the interval between sightings is doing double duty as a measurement of the cluster in front and a check on cosmic expansion.

sources.title: XPRIZE Wildfire winners spotted fires within 10 min—but couldn’t stop them

items.title: No Grand Prize in the Wildfire XPRIZE, but a 10-Minute Detection Target
items.body: The $11 million XPRIZE Wildfire competition honored finalists whose work included wildfire detection from space and firefighting drones. No team walked away with either of the two grand prizes. The First Prize track for space-based detection challenged teams to accurately detect all fires across a large swath of Australia within 10 minutes. Ars Technica notes such technology could prove helpful as wildfire disasters grow costlier.

items.title: A New Poll Finds Democrats Ahead as Midterm Voting Begins
items.body: Voting in the midterm elections is already underway, and President Trump is asking voters to pretend he is on the ballot. A new PBS News/NPR/Marist poll finds that people are — and PBS reports that could be bad news for the president, because the poll found Democratic congressional candidates hold a significant lead over Republicans. Lisa Desjardins reported the findings for PBS NewsHour.

sources.title: NASA Aircraft to Make Low-Altitude Research Flights Over Colorado

items.title: A Low-Flying Aircraft Will Sample Farm Emissions Over Greeley, Colorado
items.body: An aircraft will fly low over farmland near Greeley, Colorado, in October 2026 to measure what agriculture puts into the air. The FarmFlux mission will deploy more than a dozen sensors to measure ozone, methane, ammonia, particulates and other pollutants rising from agricultural lands and animal farms, along with how those emissions interact with the atmosphere.

sources.title: Discord age verification rolls out today with changes spurred by user backlash

items.title: Discord's Age Checks Arrive After an Earlier Plan Was Scrapped
items.body: Discord is rolling out an age-verification system that estimates each user's age and requires some users to prove they are old enough. The company had announced a somewhat different plan for age checks in February but scrapped it amid backlash from users concerned about privacy. That worry had a concrete basis: in 2025, hackers stole the government IDs of 70,000 Discord users from a third-party service. Estimating age first, and asking only some users for proof, may limit how much identity data the platform has to hold — but it does not remove the check itself.

sources.title: The stories we tell ourselves shape who we are

items.title: What Three Yoruba Names Show About Identity as a Story
items.body: Identity is anchored in stories, the argument goes: we are shaped by the stories we live in and live by. Writing in The Conversation Canada, the author points to her own three names — Olabisi, Abike and Oluwaremilekun — which, as a child, communicated deep cultural and emotional significance. Her Yoruba heritage and her grandmother's teachings, she writes, laid the foundation for her formal education and her career as a teacher. The claim is not simply that stories describe a self, but that they help constitute one — which makes what you are told about yourself early, and who tells it, more than decoration.

items.title: Iran's President Tells the UN His Country Won't Bend to U.S. Intimidation
items.body: Masoud Pezeshkian used his address to the UN General Assembly to say Iran will not yield to American intimidation. PBS NewsHour notes the timing: he spoke one day after President Trump threatened, from the same stage, to escalate the war. On the sidelines, U.S. and Iranian officials signaled no breakthroughs in mediated talks.

items.body: The Conservative Party of B.C. has confirmed that former leader John Rustad is not seeking re-election. He is not leaving alone: several other high-profile candidates have bowed out of the race, among them four former cabinet ministers from the governing B.C. NDP.

sources.title: How invideo improves color grading 3x with GPT‑6 Astra

items.title: A Threefold Color-Grading Claim, Reported by the Company That Sells the Model
items.body: OpenAI says the video-editing company invideo uses GPT-6 Astra to plan edits with greater precision, to improve color correction and grading threefold, and to turn out 50 custom effects in a single day. The figures come from the model maker's own account of a customer's workflow, which is worth remembering the next time a multiplier like that appears in a product write-up. A threefold improvement sounds like a speedometer reading, but precision, grading quality and daily output are three different things, and only one of them has a number attached.

items.body: Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat, asked Trump officials to explain why the Census Bureau's parent agency cut a ban on political interference from its scientific integrity policy, as NPR first reported.

items.body: Beijing is moving to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from leaving the country, Deutsche Welle reports. The same country that has been accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own, according to DW.

discussion.body: The shorthand is not just imprecise; it assigns Tenzing a supporting role in an event he was central to.
Reframing can overcorrect. A film that makes Tenzing the protagonist is still making a narrative choice, not delivering a neutral correction.
Both versions are stories. The real question is which one a film can make an audience feel as the truer one.

items.title: The Everest Shorthand That a New Film Wants to Undo
items.body: Variety reports that the Apple Original film “Tenzing,” opening the Zurich Film Festival, sets out to reframe the story of the first ascent of Mount Everest. Tenzing Norgay, the outlet notes, was the first person to summit Everest alongside Edmund Hillary. The film takes aim at a familiar shorthand: “Hillary conquered Everest, assisted by a Sherpa.” That framing turns a central figure into a supporting player. The reframing is the point: the movie wants the story told from Tenzing’s side of the rope.
